ORIGIN

THE PROBLEM IT SOLVES

Most health apps address one thing. Steps, or nutrition, or heart rate — never all of it in one place that's actually free. For elderly adults and people managing chronic conditions, fragmented tools aren't just inconvenient. They're dangerous. Missing a pattern across metrics because they live in three different apps is a real failure of modern health technology.

PacePal was built to close that gap — cardiovascular monitoring, step tracking, nutrition logging, hydration management, sleep analysis, and the WalkMate emergency safety system all in one free application. Designed with a faculty advisor (Dr. Visvasuresh Govindaswamy, Concordia University Chicago) over two Agile sprints and presented at the IEEE competition where it placed top 10 nationally.

FEATURES

WHAT WAS BUILT

🏠
HEALTH DASHBOARD
Overall wellness score visualized as a color-coded health ring. Five metric cards — heart, steps, sleep, hydration, recovery — each with plain-language insights.
❤️
HEART MONITORING
Resting heart rate, HRV, and recovery score from Apple Health. Plain-language interpretation of every reading — no medical jargon required.
👟
STEP TRACKER
Live step counting with real-time calorie burn, distance, and active minutes. Weekly bar chart with W/M toggle. SVG ring showing progress against dynamic goal.
🥗
NUTRITION & HYDRATION
Calorie tracking with remaining calculation, water intake logger with 250ml increment, MyFitnessPal integration, progress bars for daily targets.
🚶
WALKMATE
Designed specifically for elderly users. Step tracking, medical info storage, emergency alert system with one-tap 911 or designated contact notification.
🔗
CONNECTED APPS
Apple Health connected by default on iOS. Google Fit, StepsApp, and MyFitnessPal integration hooks. Single panel to manage all data sources.
ENGINEERING DEPTH

THE DESIGN PROCESS

PacePal was designed before a single line of code was written. A full suite of engineering artifacts was produced using Agile-Scrum methodology under Dr. Govindaswamy's advisement.

1
USE CASE DIAGRAMS
Two diagrams — authentication system and main application. Mapped every user interaction with include/extend relationships. Database actor connected to all persistence use cases.
2
HIERARCHICAL TASK ANALYSIS
Two HTA diagrams decomposing the user's mental model of the app — from Run App down through Welcome, Sign In, and all five home modules. Each branch annotated with conditional logic.
3
FINITE STATE DIAGRAM
Complete state machine — every screen as a state, every user action as a transition. Entry actions, active behaviors, and exit conditions annotated on every state.
4
SEQUENCE DIAGRAMS
Three diagrams — Sign In flow, WalkMate emergency alert flow, and home health data flow. Four actors: User, GUI, Application, Database.
5
DATA FLOW DIAGRAM
Full system DFD from launch to close. External App Databases actor. Bidirectional sync flows for Apple Health and Google Fit. Clean termination via Save & CloseApp.
6
WHITE & BLACK BOX TESTING
9 white box test functions including step goal calculation, calorie burn formula, distance conversion, health ring color logic, and WalkMate session interval. 12 black box test flows covering every user-facing screen.
